description: Linux-only local PostgreSQL and MinIO proof that an actual deletion-worker child process killed with SIGKILL after real object erasure but before database sweep cannot resurrect data and is safely recovered by lease expiry plus replacement-worker reclaim.
requiredSequence: create one synthetic epoch-1 account with a real versioned MinIO upload and canonical database object ledger
DELETE /v1/account returns 202 with durable deletion epoch 2
start an independent child test process using the same non-superuser application database role and local MinIO dependency
child process claims deletion lease at attempt 1 without receiving an account identifier from the parent
child process reads object keys from the deletion-runtime ledger and erases at least one real MinIO object version
child process signals only that claim and object erasure completed, then blocks before database sweep, completion or lease release
parent sends operating-system SIGKILL to the child and verifies WaitStatus reports SIGKILL
database ledger remains present, account remains deleting and object versions remain absent after child death
replacement claim is unavailable before lease expiry
after lease expiry replacement worker reclaims the same deletion work at attempt 2
replacement object erasure is idempotent and database sweep completes
final backlog pending and stuck counts are zero, owned rows are zero, deleted tombstone remains epoch 2 and object versions remain zero
abortCriteria: child receives an account id or object key from the parent instead of claiming and discovering work itself
child does not erase a real object version before being killed
child calls Release, Sweep or Complete before SIGKILL
process termination is not verified as SIGKILL
database ledger disappears before replacement-worker recovery
the lease becomes reclaimable before expiry
replacement receipt does not report attempt 2
any owned row or object version survives or reappears
result contains database URL, object key, account id, token, credential or process environment
limitations: SIGKILL covers one Linux child process and does not prove host, container-runtime or availability-zone failure
five-second lease is test-only and not a production lease recommendation
local PostgreSQL 16 and MinIO are not production-equivalent dependencies
one account does not establish throughput, capacity or safe operating thresholds
